summary: Recorded the honest result of the attempt to close the end-to-end limitation on the conf-change finding, plus the boundary it exposed. Driving a real three-node network did not produce a committed malformed change: because that harness never advanced the application's applied index, the leader's pendingConfIndex still exceeded raftLog.applied when the empty JointExplicit change was proposed, so the propose-time alreadyPending guard fired, the entry came out as EntryNormal, and the malformed change was dropped before replication; the later panic came from calling applyConfChange directly on the change object, which is the shortcut the limitation already flags. Recorded as a behaviour fact: the guard is about unapplied conf changes, not the transition field, and it can intercept the change whenever a configuration change is still unapplied, while appliedTo advances applied in normal operation so the guard clears once the application catches up. The interpretation is revised to explained with the defect claim still asserted and a sharper precondition (pendingConfIndex <= raftLog.applied at propose time), with the end-to-end commit demonstration explicitly left open and no claim that a clustered run reaches the panic through a genuine commit. The earlier receipts, the widened two-transition trigger and the Auto control are unchanged, and the harness limitation that the test network cannot represent an id absent from the network is noted as process knowledge, not target knowledge.
